reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates that a Ni coating on diamond particles forms a solid solution with an HEA matrix, reduces interfacial energy, fills voids, and improves mechanical properties. However, the hypothesis extends these findings to a different material system (W–Cu), a different property (thermal conductivity), and adds irradiation conditions, none of which are directly supported by the cited passages.
premises: A Ni coating on a reinforcement particle can form a solid solution or bonded interface with a matrix during sintering
Such a coating reduces interfacial energy mismatch and improves bonding strength
Improved interfacial bonding eliminates interfacial voids/cracks and increases composite density
Enhanced interfacial integrity translates to improved bulk properties (e.g., mechanical, and by extension thermal)
